lessons.title: Wind and no-go zone
lessons.goal: Find the wind and point into the no-go zone, about 45° either side of it.
lessons.blurb: The sail shakes when you point too close to the wind.

steps.say: The streaks on the water are the wind. Steer with {ls}.
Turn the bow into the wind. The arrow shows where it comes from.
Hold it. You are in the no-go zone, about 45° either side of the wind. The sail is luffing and there is no drive.

lessons.title: Stopping (lying-to)
lessons.goal: Ease the sheet and turn toward the wind until the boat lies to and stops.
lessons.blurb: Let the sail fly, then point into the wind.

steps.say: To stop, ease the sheet with {lt} until the sail luffs. Do not keep driving.
Turn the bow toward the wind with {ls}. Let the boat slow down.
Hold it. You are lying-to: the sail is luffing and the boat has nearly stopped. Bear away when you want to sail again.

lessons.title: Beam reach
lessons.goal: Sail across the wind, trim until the sail goes quiet, and keep the boat flat.
lessons.blurb: Wind on the beam. Trim the sheet. Hike the heel off.

steps.say: Bear away with {ls} until the wind is on the beam. That is a beam reach.
Sheet in with {rt} until the shaking stops. The telltales should stream aft.
If the boat heels, hold {a} and hike out to windward. A flat boat keeps its speed.

lessons.title: Points of sail
lessons.goal: Sail close-hauled, a reach, and a run. The wheel shows which one you are on.
lessons.blurb: Close hauled, a reach, then a run.

steps.say: Sail close hauled. Toward the wind, but stay outside the no-go, about 45° off it. Sheet in with {rt}.
Bear away to a reach. The wind should be on the side of the boat.
Bear away further, onto a run. Ease with {lt} so the sail stays full.

lessons.title: Tack
lessons.goal: Look around, call it, push the tiller away, and come out with speed.
lessons.blurb: Ready about, lee-oh, then bear away to build speed.

steps.say: Settle close hauled, sail full, boat moving. Look around before you tack.
Call Ready about. Call Lee-oh as you push the tiller away with {ls} and ease with {lt}.
Cross the boat facing forward. Change hands. {b} brings you in, then {a} hikes you out on the new windward side.
Bear away slightly and sheet in with {rt} so the boat builds speed on the new tack.

lessons.title: Out of irons
lessons.goal: The boat is stopped, head to wind. Fall off, fill the sail, and sail again.
lessons.blurb: No drive. Push the tiller so the bow falls off the wind.

steps.say: You are in irons, no drive. Push the tiller with {ls} so the bow falls off the wind. Wait for the boat to move.
The bow is off. Sheet in with {rt} and bear away a little more until the sail draws.

lessons.title: Return to the pontoon
lessons.goal: Approach on a reach, depowered, and luff up alongside at walking pace.
lessons.blurb: Slow approach. Keep an escape route. Never fend off.

steps.say: Approach on a close reach or a reach. Ease with {lt} so the sail is depowered. Walking pace, not a charge.
Luff up alongside with {ls}. Keep an escape route. If you are too fast, bear away and go round again. Never fend off with your hands or your feet.
Stopped, within a metre, {rb} makes fast. If the boat is still driving, abort and go round.

lessons.title: Gybe (extra)
lessons.goal: Bear away to a run, check the area, call gybe-oh, and duck.
lessons.blurb: Extra. A controlled gybe, and a by-the-lee warning.

steps.say: Bear away to a run. Ease with {lt}. Look behind the sail and check the area is clear.
Call Gybe-oh. Help the boom across, DUCK, bring the tiller to the centre, change sides, and straighten up.
Straighten up on the new gybe. If the wind is on the same side as the boom you are by the lee, and the boom can crash across. Steer so the wind stays on the windward side.

lessons.title: Capsize (extra)
lessons.goal: Know why a dinghy capsizes, and what you do when it does.
lessons.blurb: Extra. Ease the sheet. Stay with the boat.

steps.say: A capsize comes from too much sail, a hike held through a lull, or a gybe that rolls you. Ease the sheet early.
If you capsize, stay with the boat. It floats. Climb onto the centreboard and right it. Do not swim for shore.
Once it is up, bail, count the crew, and sail only when everyone is back aboard.

lessons.title: Safety
lessons.goal: Four things before you leave the shore.
lessons.blurb: Lifejacket, forecast, a person ashore, stay with the boat.

steps.say: Wear a lifejacket before you leave the shore. Clip it. This is not optional.
Check the forecast. If the wind is rising or a storm is due, stay ashore.
Tell someone ashore where you are going and when you will be back.
If you capsize or fall in, stay with the boat. A dinghy is easier to see than a person.

lessons.title: Man overboard
lessons.goal: The basics if someone goes in the water.
lessons.blurb: Shout, point, keep them in sight, and stop the boat.

steps.say: Shout and point. Do not jump in after them. One person in the water is enough.
Keep the person in sight. Throw a line or anything that floats if you have it.
Sail back on a reach, stop to windward of them, and help them in. Stay with the boat.

lessons.title: Right of way
lessons.goal: Three rules that keep boats apart.
lessons.blurb: Port gives way. Windward gives way. The overtaker keeps clear.

steps.say: A boat on port tack gives way to a boat on starboard tack.
The windward boat gives way to the leeward boat.
The overtaking boat keeps clear. These are the basics, not a substitute for the real rules.
